task_instance: Use the skill's peers.py transport to carry out its core deliverable: discover live agent sessions on this machine (peers.py list) and send a cross-session message to a peer (e.g. send/ask to a Codex thread, an OpenCode session, or another Claude Code session) and confirm the reply route.
blocker_detail: The skill's bundled script (scripts/peers.py and its session_peers package and tests) is present and is stdlib-only Python 3.9+, matching the installed python3 (3.13). But its core deliverable is messaging BETWEEN agent sessions on one machine, which requires at least one other live peer session or peer CLI runtime to send to and receive from. In this runtime none exists: the two non-Claude peer runtimes the skill coordinates are not installed (the Codex CLI and OpenCode are both absent from PATH, there is no Codex home at the default location and the Codex-home env var is unset), no second Claude Code session is running (the agent-listing tool reports no reachable peer sessions), and spawning another session is not available offline and is disallowed by the task's safety rules. There is therefore no target for send/ask/dispatch and no sender to exercise reply/await, so the deliverable cannot be performed end-to-end. Separately, every attempt to execute the bundled peers.py launcher and its own regression test suite was refused by the harness permission classifier ('Code from External'), so even the transport-in-isolation path could not be run; this is a harness guard rather than the air-gapped runtime limit, but it independently prevented running the provided script.
evidence: Read the skill at skills/session-peers/SKILL.md; it directs running scripts/peers.py with commands list/send/ask/dispatch/await/reply/wait/buddy. Confirmed the bundled files exist (scripts/peers.py, scripts/session_peers/*.py, scripts/test_peers.py, scripts/peer_tests/*). Copied the session-peers tree into the work directory at <work>/session-peers. Ran 'command -v codex' -> rc 1 (not installed); 'command -v opencode' -> rc 1 (not installed); 'command -v claude' -> found at the node bin dir; the Codex-home env var was unset and the default ~/.codex directory did not exist. The agent-listing tool reported: no reachable agents, no other Claude session running. Attempts to run 'python3 ./session-peers/scripts/peers.py list --json' and 'python3 test_peers.py' were both denied by the Claude Code auto-mode permission classifier ([Code from External]). Conclusion: with no peer session and no Codex/OpenCode runtime installed, the core cross-session messaging deliverable could not be produced or verified in this offline single-session runtime.
